description: A sawtooth and square oscillator modelled on an ageing analogue circuit, where a drying capacitor bends the sawtooth into a shark fin

params.text: Sets the frequency, four octaves either side of C4 at 261.63Hz
Sets how old the circuit is, from 0 to 40 years; age lifts the two high-pass corners that bend the wave and adds gain to make up the bass it loses
Switches between the sawtooth and the square on each press

inputs.text: Adds to the frequency knob at 1V per octave, with the total held between four octaves below C4 and six above
A rising edge switches between the sawtooth and the square
Adds to the age at four years per volt, with the total clamped between 0 and 60 years

outputs.text: The wave, high-passed by the ageing circuit, soft-clipped and stripped of DC

notes: the red lamp is lit for the sawtooth and the blue lamp for the square; the choice is saved with the patch, and Rack's randomise picks one of the two at random.
the square is played at 0.7 of the sawtooth's level so that the two sound about as loud as each other.
the module runs at four times the sample rate below a 50kHz engine rate, twice above that and once above 100kHz.
the green lamp flashes at a twentieth of the oscillator's frequency.
the AGE knob draws a gold arc from its own position round to where its CV input has moved it, and the arc turns orange when the CV pushes the age past 0 or 60 years.

inputs.1: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.2:
continuous · polyphonic

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
